title: Programming and reprogramming the nervous system via CUT homeobox genes
abstract: Abstract Background: A central question in neurobiology is how the transcriptional programs that define a neuron are established in development and held stable thereafter. The CUT homeobox genes offer an unusually revealing window onto this problem. Summary: We review the function of the CUX and ONECUT families across phyla: dosage-dependent control of sensory fate and dendritic morphology in flies, redundant maintenance of pan-neuronal identity in the nematode, and combinatorial neuronal subtype specification in the vertebrate cortex, retina and spinal cord. We then examine how the same factors are deployed in neuronal reprogramming, acting as both exogenous drivers and endogenously recruited effectors, following a recurrent hierarchy from proneural initiation to CUT-mediated specification. Key Messages. By tracing CUT function from invertebrate sensory circuits to vertebrate reprogramming, this review positions invertebrate models as tractable entry points for dissecting how neuronal identity is built and restored.
